1. Realistic assessment of the route

A C1 professional in Arabic standard requires about 2.300–2.500 actual hours. Studying alone an hour a day is about 8 years; intensively paced, tutor and at least one dive period you go down to 4–5 years. None of these figures is a guarantee. The most solid reference. The US Department of State Foreign Service Institute places Arabic in category IV, the most difficult: 88 weeks, 2.200 hours of class, to bring an English-speaking diplomat to ...General Professional Proficiency (ILR Speaking-3/Reading-3). It is hours in the full-time classroom, with native speakers and additional evening study (source: state.gov/foreeign-language-training). For an italophone the distance is similar: the Italian does not offer shortcuts on writing, morphology or vocabulary, except a few loans. ILR 3 corresponds to broad lines at C1, but the correspondence is not official. During the course we use the CEFR scale for teaching and keep an eye on ILR/STANAG because it is used in defence and security. Hours available. Calculation on 365 days, removing a 20% for shifts, tiredness and unexpectedness.
Orientation mats. The cumulative hours are teaching estimates built on the FSI data, not measures; the time is taken on regular study.

2. Language strategy

Modern standard Arabic (MSA) as a carrier axis from day one; Egyptian as the first dialect, listening passively from A2 and systematic study by B1; a Maghrebine variety in passive understanding from B2. The choice of dialect is confirmed at the end A2.
2.1 Core: Modern Standard Arabic

MSA (al-ʿarabiyya al-fuṣḥā al-muʿāṣira) is the language of newspapers, official press releases, news, documents and most of the online institutional texts. No one speaks it as a mother tongue, but every educated person reads it. Classical Arabic (Koran, ancient literature) shares with the MSA grammar and writing; They mostly change vocabulary and style. Also the external evidence you are interested in is in MSA: the CIMA of the Institut du monde arabe evaluates only the Arab standard (imarabe.org), and the Italian JFLT for Arabic, used in defense according to STANAG 6001, is built in MSA for all four skills (study published by Roma TrE-Press, University Roma Tre).
2.2 Dialectal varieties in comparison
The dialects are distinct spoken languages, not wrong: they differ in sounds, grammar and vocabulary, and the mutual understanding between Morocco and Iraq is limited.

2.3 Recommended Choice
1. First dialect: Egyptian. It's the most understood everywhere, has the best resources after MSA, has a distance
moderated by the standard and in Milan gives you real opportunities for listening and conversation.
2. Second variety, only understanding: maghrebina. Tunisian and Libyan if your job looks at the
Mediterranean and migration flows; Moroccan if it remains on national territory.
3. Levantino passive through interviews and television debates, without formal study, from B2.

Final decision point A2. If at that moment your trajectory points to analysis on Syria, Lebanon or Jordan, the first dialect becomes the Levantine; the timetable does not change, because the systematic study starts only at B1.

blocks.text: Anti-interference rules:
• Separate Anki decks and labels [MSA] / [EGY] on each card; never mix the two shapes in the same paper,
except in comparison cards.
• For each point of dialect grammar, a table contrasting with the MSA (denial, future, demonstration,
pronouns, high frequency vocabulary).
• Separate sessions: a block is either ... or ... or ...EGY... never both.
• It is always written in MSA, except for explicit reading exercises of written dialect.
2.5 Professional skills beyond the language
These skills enter the curriculum as dedicated tracks, because a generic translator does not own them:
• Unvocalised reading and ambiguity management. Trained by Level 0: the same spelling can
correspond to several words, and the analyst must state which reading he chooses and why.
• Translation, synthesis, interpretation. Three separate operations: the translation renders the text; the summary of
reduces content without adding; the explicit interpretation of the implications and must always be marked as such.
• Verbs of attribution and degree of certainty. ........
in Arabic are precise lexical choices that indicate the position of the writer.
• Arab name and transliteration of names. Name structure (ism, nasab, kunya, laqab, nisba) and

variants: the same name appears as Mohamed, Muhammad or Mohammed; the names of the Maghrebini pass from the French spelling (Abdelkader to ʿAbd al-Qādir); the Egyptian makes ⁧ج⁩ with g (Gamal for Ǧamāl).
• Arabic and Arab social media. Many informal messages use Latin characters and digits: 2 = ⁧ء⁩ , 3 = ⁧ع⁩ , 5 = ⁧خ⁩ , 7 = ⁧ح⁩ ;
on 9 value ⁧ق⁩ or ⁧ص⁩ Depending on the region. The written dialect has no fixed spelling.
• Work on open sources. Comparison of sources, distinction between facts and opinions, explicit declaration of limits and
the degree of certainty. The entire specialist module works on public materials and with the purpose of linguistic analysis: no operational or surveillance techniques.

6.5 Advanced and tutor mode

The progress log is in the Excel file: a line for lesson with date, scores, time spent and notes on errors. It is the source of truth, independent from any memory of the platform. To study with me in tutoring mode, write "Session" followed by the lesson code (e.g. Session L0-02() and paste the last line of the register. The session always follows these steps:
1. I identify the lesson and briefly resume the previous one.
2. Checking with 3–5 Quick questions what you should already know.
3. I explain the new topic with examples.
4. I'll give you the exercises one at a time and wait for your answer: I don't show you the solution before, unless you request it.
5. I correct by explaining the cause of the error, then propose a consolidation exercise on the same point.
6. At the end of the session I will give you the updated line of the log and the targeted review for the following days.
If gaps in the initial check-up appear on the basics, the session returns to those before adding new material.
